title: Sport and leisure
subtitle: play football, go swimming, do a bit of yoga
summary: Name sports, the people who do them and the places they happen, and choose between play, go and do.

lesson.heading: Sports, people and verbs
lesson.note: Most sports are also verbs: a skier skis, a boxer boxes, a sailor sails.

lesson.heading: play, go or do?
lesson.text: We **play** sports such as football, ice hockey, tennis, golf and basketball. We use **go** with other sports and activities, especially those ending in *-ing*. We use **do** with *a lot of* or *a bit of* + *-ing*.

examples.text: I **play** football in the winter. I **play** basketball twice a week.
I **go** swimming in the lake during summer. We often **go** rock climbing in the mountains.
I **did a bit of** sailing in the holidays.
I don't **do a lot of** running these days.

lesson.heading: Where you do it
rows: on the sea or a lake

lesson.heading: Equipment
lesson.text: Every sport needs its own equipment. A football goal has a **net**, an ice hockey player uses a **stick**, a skier wears **skis**, and a swimmer needs a **swimming costume**. The player who stands in the goal is the **goalkeeper**.

examples.text: The ball went straight into the **net**.
If the girls go swimming, they must remember to take their **swimming costumes**.
The **goalkeeper** stopped the ball with one hand.

lesson.heading: Leisure activities
lesson.text: Leisure activities are the things you do in your free time: **camping**, **rock climbing**, **jogging**, **yoga** and **going to the gym**. You need a **tent** if you want to go camping.

examples.text: We often **go camping** in the summer, and we usually **do a bit of rock climbing** as well.
My best friend **does a lot of yoga**.

lesson.heading: Keeping fit
lesson.text: If exercise **keeps you fit**, it helps your body to stay in good condition. You can also **work out** in the gym. If you do something **for fun** or **for pleasure**, you do it because you enjoy it, not because it is serious.

examples.text: My brother enjoys jogging, and it **keeps him fit**.
I used to **work out** in the gym, but I'm getting a bit old for that now.
My dad plays golf. He's not a serious golfer; he just plays **for fun**.
I'm afraid I don't **do any exercise** at all.

lesson.text: Remember the three verbs: *play* + ball games, *go* + activities ending in *-ing*, *do* + *a bit of* / *a lot of*.

exercises.prompt: I ___ basketball in the summer and winter.
exercises.explanation: We play ball games such as basketball, football and tennis.

exercises.prompt: We used to ___ camping in the mountains.
exercises.explanation: We use go with activities ending in -ing, such as camping and swimming.
We do exercise; we do a lot of or a bit of an activity.

exercises.prompt: Is each word a sport, a person or a place?
Match each sport with the person who does it.
I ___ a bit of yoga when I was younger.
exercises.explanation: We use do with a bit of or a lot of + an activity.

exercises.prompt: I ___ a lot of swimming in the summer.
exercises.explanation: a lot of swimming takes do, not go.

exercises.prompt: Equipment or place? Put each word in the right group.
If you want to keep ___, you need to run three or four miles every other day.
exercises.explanation: keep fit = stay in good physical condition.

exercises.prompt: We played golf in Scotland, where they have some fantastic golf ___.
exercises.explanation: You play golf on a golf course. A court is for basketball or tennis.

exercises.prompt: You can't go camping unless you have a ___.
exercises.explanation: A tent is the basic piece of equipment for camping.

exercises.prompt: My dad plays golf. He's not a serious golfer; he just plays for ___.
exercises.explanation: for fun = for pleasure, because you enjoy it.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence about the gym.
exercises.answer: I used to work out in the gym every week
exercises.explanation: work out = do exercise, usually in a gym.

exercises.statement: Running is good exercise, so four or five times a week I go jogging.
exercises.explanation: Correct. We say go jogging, like go swimming and go camping.
